key_insight: VQE’s adversarial robustness is highly uneven: attacks that tamper with the noise/ZNE pipeline are the most damaging, while parameter backdoors are comparatively weak.
engineering_relevance: For cloud VQE deployments, security must cover the full stack—transpilation, runtime, co-tenancy, and error-mitigation—not just the quantum circuit itself.
method: Built VQE-AdvBench, a unified red-teaming benchmark for VQE adversarial robustness
Classified threats by black-, gray-, and white-box access
Evaluated seven attack scenarios across H2 and H3+ on five noise-calibrated IBM backends
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, noise-induced QNBAD variants amplified energy error by up to 8.84×, QTrojan reached 7.52×, and QDoor peaked at only 1.37×.
watch_item: Results are tied to specific molecules, ansatzes, backends, and a fixed evaluation protocol, so severity may shift for other VQE settings or mitigation choices.
paper_title: SoK: Adversarial Robustness of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver via Red-Teaming
